ui.intro: Open one door a day, from the first Sunday of Advent to Christmas Eve. Behind each one is that day’s date, a verse from Scripture, a short reflection and one small thing to do. The doors you open are remembered on this device.
ui.art: A snowy stone church at night with {n} numbered doors and windows, one for each day of Advent
ui.wait: Not yet! This door opens on {d}. Advent is a season of waiting, so come back then.
ui.before: Advent begins on {d}. The first door, high in the bell tower, opens that day.
ui.after: Merry Christmas! Every door is open now, so read any day again. Christmas is a whole season, all the way to the Baptism of the Lord.
ui.hint: Tap a numbered door. Today’s door glows.

sundays.q: Take heed, watch; for you do not know when the time will come.
sundays.r: A new Church year begins today. Light the first violet candle on the Advent wreath, the candle of hope. Jesus asks us to stay awake: not anxious, but ready, like a family waiting up for someone they love to come home.
sundays.a: Set up an Advent wreath, or simply light one candle tonight and pray together.

sundays.q: In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
sundays.r: Light two candles today. John the Baptist calls out from the desert: prepare the way of the Lord. Every crooked path in us, every grudge and every habit we keep excusing, is a road God wants to make straight.
sundays.a: Choose one thing to straighten out before Christmas, and start today.

sundays.q: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, Rejoice.… The Lord is at hand.
sundays.r: This is Gaudete Sunday, from the Latin for “rejoice.” Light the rose candle, and look for rose vestments at Mass. We are more than halfway there, and joy breaks through the waiting because the Lord is near.
sundays.a: Do something just for joy today: sing, visit a friend, laugh, celebrate.

sundays.q: Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.
sundays.r: Light all four candles. Today we stand with Mary, a young woman who said yes to God without knowing everything that would follow. Her yes opened the door for Christ to come into the world.
sundays.a: Pray a Hail Mary slowly, and ask for the grace to say yes to God.

11-27.q: But watch at all times, praying that you may have strength … to stand before the Son of man.
11-27.r: Advent begins by waking us up. Jesus will come again, and he comes to us every day: in prayer, in the Mass and in people in need. Watching for him is not fear. It is love that leaves the porch light on.
11-27.a: Pick one time each day this Advent for five quiet minutes with God.

11-28.q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who dwelt in a land of deep darkness, on them has light shined.
11-28.r: The nights are long at this time of year, and Advent knows it. Whatever darkness you are carrying, the promise stands: a light is coming that the darkness cannot put out.
11-28.a: Light a candle at dinner tonight and pray for someone who is struggling.

11-29.q: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.… And God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
11-29.r: Many families walk through the whole Bible story in Advent, from Creation to Bethlehem. It begins here: everything that exists is God’s gift, made good and made out of love, and that includes you.
11-29.a: Step outside and thank God for three things he made.

11-30.q: “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
11-30.r: Andrew was a fisherman who met Jesus and right away brought his brother Peter to meet him too. Today many Catholics begin the Saint Andrew Christmas prayer, said fifteen times a day until Christmas.
11-30.a: Invite one person to something good: Mass, a meal, a real conversation.

12-01.q: I set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
12-01.r: After the flood, God promised never to give up on his people, and he hung a rainbow in the sky to say so. Every promise of Advent rests on this one: God keeps his word.
12-01.a: Think of a promise you have made, and keep it today.

12-02.q: “Look toward heaven, and number the stars, if you are able to number them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your descendants be.”
12-02.r: Abraham was old and had no children, yet God told him to look up and count the stars. He trusted, and from his family came Jesus. When a hope seems impossible, look up.
12-02.a: Tonight, find a star and tell God the hope you are carrying.

12-03.q: Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!
12-03.r: Francis Xavier sailed from Europe to India and Japan to share the Gospel, often exhausted and far from home. He is a patron of missionaries, and a reminder that good news is meant to be shared.
12-03.a: Pray for missionaries, or tell someone what your faith means to you.

12-04.q: Where you go I will go, and where you lodge I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
12-04.r: Ruth was a foreigner who stayed loyal to her widowed mother-in-law, and she became the great-grandmother of King David. Jesus’ family tree has room for outsiders, and so does his Church.
12-04.a: Reach out to someone who is new, alone or far from home.

12-05.q: For the LORD sees not as man sees; man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.
12-05.r: When God sent Samuel to choose a king, he passed over the tall, impressive brothers and chose the youngest, out in the fields with the sheep. Jesus would be born in David’s town and called the Son of David.
12-05.a: Notice someone others overlook, and thank them.

12-06.q: When you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing, so that your alms may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
12-06.r: Nicholas, a bishop in what is now Turkey, is remembered for secret gifts, like gold left at night for a poor family. He is the real saint behind Santa Claus, and children set out their shoes for him.
12-06.a: Give something in secret today, and take no credit.

12-07.q: Thy word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
12-07.r: Ambrose was the governor of Milan when the people chose him as their bishop, before he was even baptized. His preaching helped lead Saint Augustine to faith. God’s word, heard faithfully, changes lives.
12-07.a: Read tomorrow’s Gospel slowly before bed.

12-08.q: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you!
12-08.r: Today the Church celebrates that Mary, from the first moment of her life, was kept free from sin by God’s grace, to be the mother of his Son. She is the patroness of the United States under this title.
12-08.a: It is a holy day of obligation in the U.S.: go to Mass today, or at a vigil Mass last evening.
12-08.a_moved: This year it is kept on Monday, December 9, without the obligation. Go to Mass if you can, and pray a Hail Mary slowly.

12-09.q: He has put down the mighty from their thrones, and exalted those of low degree.
12-09.r: Juan Diego was a humble Indigenous man in Mexico to whom Mary appeared in 1531, asking for a church to be built. He worried he was too small for the task. She chose him for exactly that reason.
12-09.a: Pray for someone who feels unimportant, and tell them they matter.

12-10.t: Our Lady of Loreto: the holy house
12-10.q: And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them; and his mother kept all these things in her heart.
12-10.r: Loreto in Italy honors the house of Nazareth, where Jesus grew up in an ordinary home with Mary and Joseph. God chose to be close to us in kitchens, chores and family life.
12-10.a: Bless your home: walk through it and pray for everyone who lives there.

12-11.q: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
12-11.r: These words were first spoken to people in exile who thought God had forgotten them. They are spoken to you too. Advent is God speaking tenderly to tired hearts.
12-11.a: Write a short note of comfort to someone who is grieving or worn out.

12-12.q: And a great portent appeared in heaven, a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
12-12.r: In 1531 Mary appeared at Tepeyac in Mexico as a young expectant mother, dressed like the people of the land, and left her image on Juan Diego’s cloak. She is the patroness of the Americas and of unborn children.
12-12.a: Pray for mothers expecting a child, and for every child waiting to be born.

12-13.q: You are the light of the world.… Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.
12-13.r: Lucy, whose name means “light,” was a young Christian in Sicily who gave her wealth to the poor and died for her faith around the year 304. In Sweden, girls in white with crowns of candles honor her at dawn.
12-13.a: Do one good deed today that lets your light shine.

12-14.q: God is love, and he who abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him.
12-14.r: John was a Spanish Carmelite friar, once imprisoned by his own brothers, who wrote some of the most beautiful poems ever written about God’s love. He taught that in the evening of life we will be judged on love.
12-14.a: Before bed, ask yourself: where did I love well today?

12-15.q: Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; yea, wait for the LORD!
12-15.r: Waiting is hard: in lines, in hospitals, for answers that do not come. Advent turns waiting into prayer. God is not late. He is preparing something, and he is with you while you wait.
12-15.a: The next time you have to wait today, pray instead of scrolling.

12-16.q: She gave birth to her first-born son and wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.
12-16.r: Tonight Simbang Gabi begins, the Filipino nine days of Masses, and so does Las Posadas, when neighbors walk with Mary and Joseph knocking on doors for shelter. Both ask one question: will I make room for him?
12-16.a: Make room: clear a little time for prayer, or give to a shelter.

12-17.q: I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth like a mist.
12-17.r: Today the “O Antiphons” begin: seven ancient titles for Jesus, sung in the last week before Christmas. The first calls him the Wisdom that comes from the mouth of God and orders all things with strength and gentleness.
12-17.a: Sing or read the first verse of “O Come, O Come, Emmanuel.”

12-18.q: The angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush; and he looked, and lo, the bush was burning, yet it was not consumed.
12-18.r: Adonai means “Lord.” The God who spoke to Moses from the burning bush and set his people free from slavery is the same God who comes at Christmas to set us free.
12-18.a: Pray for anyone you know who is trapped: by addiction, debt or fear.

12-19.q: There shall come forth a shoot from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots.
12-19.r: Jesse’s family tree looked cut down to a stump, but God made a new shoot grow from it: Jesus. When something in your life seems finished, God can still bring new life.
12-19.a: Pray for your family, living and dead, by name.

12-20.q: I will place on his shoulder the key of the house of David; he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.
12-20.r: A calendar of doors, and today’s antiphon is about a key! Jesus is the Key of David, who opens what no one can shut. He opens the way to heaven and sets free those who sit in darkness.
12-20.a: Ask Jesus to open one door in your life that seems locked.

12-21.q: For you who fear my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings.
12-21.r: In the northern half of the world this is about the darkest day of the year, and on it the Church sings to Jesus, the Dawn, the Sun of justice. From now on the days grow longer, and Christmas is very near.
12-21.a: Watch the sunrise or the sunset, and pray for those who sit in darkness.

12-22.q: For to us a child is born, to us a son is given; and the government will be upon his shoulder, and his name will be called “Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.”
12-22.r: Jesus is the King every people longs for, the cornerstone who makes two into one. His rule is not power over people but peace among them.
12-22.a: Make peace with someone, or pray for a part of the world at war.

12-23.q: Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
12-23.r: The last antiphon calls Jesus Emmanuel, “God with us.” Read the first letters of the seven Latin titles backwards and they spell ero cras: “Tomorrow I will be there.”
12-23.a: Make room in your heart before tomorrow: go to Confession if you can.

12-24.q: Be not afraid; for behold, I bring you good news of a great joy which will come to all the people; for to you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
12-24.r: The last door is the great door. Tonight the Church celebrates the birth of Jesus, and every door is open: come as you are. Christmas is not one day but a whole season, so the joy is only beginning.
12-24.a: Go to Christmas Mass tonight or tomorrow, and bring someone with you. Merry Christmas!
